assessment: The observations establish unmet requests, uneven demand, unreliable access records and variable administration. They do not establish whether existing capacity can satisfy actual needs: acceptable alternatives, equipment requirements and total durations are missing. Recoverable slack remains a hypothesis.

openings.claim: Speculative capability: construct a weekly room calendar from protected 60-minute access entitlements plus additional rehearsal time, matching each group's declared acceptable windows, equipment and required uninterrupted duration instead of automatically inheriting 90-minute reservations.
openings.delta: The scheduling unit becomes a group's rehearsal requirement and minimum entitlement, rather than its previous reservation. Dependencies are complete requirements gathered by short conversations, fixed performance reservations, explicit acceptance of any shortened or separated sessions, and one authoritative desk record with confirmed updates to its copy. The presently testable partial capability is a manually constructed feasible calendar.
openings.prediction: If inherited reservation shapes and undisclosed alternatives cause some exclusions, a requirements-based draft will satisfy more stated rehearsal needs than the inherited calendar under identical capacity and performance commitments. If acceptable windows and equipment are too concentrated, the draft will expose remaining infeasibility.
openings.probe: Ask all twelve contacts for weekly needs, acceptable windows, equipment and minimum uninterrupted duration. Compare inherited and manually reassigned calendars against those same requirements, protecting every requested weekly entitlement and both performances within the existing rooms and opening hours. Count full need satisfaction separately from minimum access. If feasible, confirm assignments by telephone or in person and track eight weeks of actual needs met, conflicts and all administrative minutes against the stated thresholds.
assumptions: Some groups accept alternatives or shorter sessions; this is unverified and must be elicited.
Additional time counts as useful only when it meets the group's declared rehearsal requirements.
Manual requirement collection and confirmation may exceed the administration budget; the probe must count that work.
The proposal uses existing equipment, introduces no fees, and requires no participant digital account.
